title: Snapdragon X Elite: Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct original Q4_K_M Janas and native llama.cpp measurements
scope: Single Windows ARM64 laptop; short fixed code and prose workloads. All final fresh/warm Janas samples and native llama.cpp baseline outcomes are retained. Functional checks are separate from throughput measurements.
path_policy: Project paths are relative; portable toolchains use toolchain-cache/ labels. Machine-specific user profile paths and OS process/thread identifiers are omitted. Measurement values and recorded hashes are preserved.

hardware.os_execution: Native Windows ARM64; WSL used for cross-building and host checks, not timed model inference

janas.source_state: Working-tree builds include local Snapdragon changes; version contains dirty. Per-case/manifest executable SHA-256 identities distinguish final and pre-Q6_K_P builds.
janas.cpu_kernels: NEON with DOTPROD; final build adds missing Q6_K_P expert down-projection dispatch

llama_cpp.cpu_build_note: Dedicated CPU + FP16 build, DOTPROD and I8MM enabled. REPACK is compiled in but disabled for these runs; the signed NPU runtime was preserved.

CatalogSignature.Subject: CN=Local GGML HTP d1d3c33 test build

hexagon_runtime.packaging_note: HardwareInferenceTested=false is packaging-time status. Subsequent real Janas NPU inference is evidenced below by successful completed-product deltas; setup/prepared-plan counts alone are not execution proof.

models.name: Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct
models.precision: Original Q4_K_M quantized weights; Janas planes preserve original quantized bits. HIGH quality, expert bits 6, head bits 0, no expert skipping.

jns_mtp_sidecar.note: Separate Q4_K MTP heads; official main GGUF omits them. Janas reports the distinct sidecar cache separately.

models.verification: Full SHA-256 checked at payload download. Benchmark manifests retain first-MiB identity checks to avoid rereading and warming the entire payload immediately before timing.

protocol.comparison_workload: Exact same frozen ChatML code prompt. A metadata-only GGUF vocabulary probe matched all 276 input token IDs and their SHA-256 to Janas; no inference was needed for this check.
protocol.janas_fresh_and_warm: One fresh process per case; each sample has a fresh conversation. Warm samples reuse the process/model expert cache, without prompt KV reuse. Selected case has three measured warm samples; most cases have one.
protocol.llama_fresh_processes: Two completed CPU8 processes, no repacking, mmap, no warmup. Private engine state is fresh; shared OS file cache is uncontrolled.
protocol.cpu_budget: Windows process affinity restricted to low N logical CPUs and requested worker/batch threads N; inherited affinity verified for llama processes.
protocol.concurrency: Final timing cases ran sequentially while other model inference, builds, and large downloads were idle.

kv_precision.janas_default: custom INT8 plus FP32 scale per KV head and position
kv_precision.precision_relation: llama KV is higher precision; cache representations are not identical

protocol.janas_rate: 128 output tokens / output_seconds; input/prefill separately recorded.
protocol.llama_rate: Primary-source printed decode rate is 127 post-prefill evaluation runs / decode milliseconds. 404 sampler accepts include 276 prompt accepts, leaving 128 generated accepts. The first output follows prefill.
protocol.cache_counters: Sample scalar expert counters are deltas; nested expert_cache counters are cache-lifetime snapshots. Main and distinct MTP sidecar caches are separately reported and totaled without double counting embedded MTP.
protocol.io_scope: Logical expert-file read bytes and cache-read wall time are not physical SSD traffic or throughput.
protocol.accelerator_counters: Sample counters are successful inference completion deltas, prepared plans are setup, and npu_weight_bytes is a current resident after-value gauge. Counters cover the whole sample.
protocol.peak_rss: Process-lifetime high-watermark; warm samples inherit earlier peaks.
protocol.accelerator_verification_applicability: CPU-only cases request no accelerator, so their accelerator_execution_verified boolean is vacuously true. A GPU/NPU speed claim additionally requires nonzero successful completion counters for every measured sample.

summary.selection_note: Three-warm confirmation is selected over the larger single-warm screen result. Best tested practical configuration for this fixed code workload, not a global optimum.

non_speculative_kernel_comparison.scope: Same 128-token code output hash, CPU8/cache32, no speculation; compares the Q6_K_P CPU dispatch change in these builds.

npu_case.outcome: Genuine NPU execution, slower than selected CPU/MTP on this workload; not NPU-only inference.

limits: One laptop and model with short fixed prompts; broad Snapdragon compatibility and sustained/long-context performance are not established.
Prose warm rates are 12.6365766 without speculation and 12.6470665 with MTP4. Code speculation gains do not generalize to all text.
Lookup reuses ngrams in the current conversation. No persistent external ngram lookup table was benchmarked.
Janas warm expert-cache samples and llama fresh processes have different private cache lifetimes. OS file cache is uncontrolled; fresh does not mean cold SSD.
llama F16 KV is higher precision than Janas custom INT8 KV. Same original weights, prompt bytes/token IDs, context, and greedy limit do not establish identical arithmetic or output across engines.
Output hashes demonstrate repeatability of measured greedy text, not comprehensive model quality. Hash agreement alone is not a quality evaluation.
Final GPU startup self-check rejected the current machine/runtime state. GPU and combined GPU/NPU configurations have no eligible final speed result here.
The CPU12 llama attempt has no completed generation/perf counters and is unranked, not a zero-TPS result. Cause remains unknown.
post_measurement_validation_notes: A post-run native parent-environment check found JANAS_KV and JANAS_ATTN absent. The older recorded manifests did not list these keys. Updated harness/launcher clear inherited overrides to architecture defaults and the harness records null. No recorded timings were changed or rerun.
Updated harness prevents a nonrepeatable CPU reference from conferring recommendation eligibility. Recorded final output signatures were stable.
Harness 19 and launcher 14 focused tests passed on both WSL and native Windows ARM64 (33 total each).
Build header probes use actual CFLAGS and require ggml-hexagon.h; focused shell/preprocessor/early-error checks passed. No new model timing.
